findings.finding: The frozen predicate (pointer-bind.py:43-47, plans/round-79-claims.md:85-86, .ufo/waves/round-79/claims.json:22 and :25) names `python3 -I -B tools/round-79/pointer-bind.py --root . --rev <measured> --json-out <receipt>` as the command that "exits 0". The CLI requires --battery: pointer-bind.py:319-321 returns 2 with a usage line when it is absent. Run verbatim at the freeze, it exits 2 and writes no receipt.
findings.evidence: evidence/c2-predicate-as-frozen.txt; instrument PREDICATE constant line 43; claims.json:22 counting_command and :25 predicate
findings.impact: The stated verification command cannot verify the claim; every auditor who follows the frozen sentence gets "could not evaluate", not the claimed exit 0. The underlying measurement is sound (my --battery run reproduces base 3/2 and freeze 5/0), so this is a frozen-text defect, not a false measurement.
findings.remediation: Add --battery to the counting_command and predicate text (record edit by the L1), or make --battery the default when --rev is present.

findings.finding: line_sha256 is computed at pointer-bind.py:105 before the token test, so a mismatched check also retains a sha256 of the live line at the stale line number (base omp-pin :8 and kimi-pin :4126). It is a digest, never bytes, and the bound permits a pointed line digest; but it is a digest of a line the check rejects, i.e. evidence the claim does not use.
findings.evidence: evidence/pb-base.json (both mismatch checks carry a 64-hex line_sha256 equal to the live stale-line digest; verified in memory); evidence/receipt-field-inventory.json digest_checks
findings.impact: No content exposure; a low-entropy stale-line digest is an offline guess oracle, and it contradicts the minimal-evidence rule.
findings.remediation: Set line_sha256 only after matched (or rename it mismatch_line_sha256 and document it); one-line move.

findings.finding: Neither instrument has a containment guard for --work/--json-out (no commonpath, is_relative_to or realpath check; grep confirms). A caller can create gate-mutation-* under /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin (fleet root), /tmp or a sibling lane, and --json-out truncates any named file. pointer-bind has no --work but the same unrestricted --json-out.
findings.impact: Only reachable by the caller that already holds the argv; the wave prompts pin the scratch and evidence dirs, so the round is not affected. It is a defence-in-depth gap: a mistyped relative --work lands in the fleet root because seat tools start there.
findings.remediation: Reject --work/--json-out outside an explicit --allow-root (lane root plus /fast/scratch), or document that the caller owns containment.

findings.finding: Field-by-field review finds no field that can carry a client-config line, an env value or a credential. The only pointed-line string that appears verbatim in a pointer-bind receipt is the Ghidra application.version=12.1.4 token, which is the record's own declared token (the pointed line is exactly that 26-character string). The .bashrc range lines (111 chars) and the pin lines in the devin/omp/kimi configs do not appear; only the pin, the key names and line digests do. gate-mutation carries no file content, no env and no stderr in a normal run; its conditional stderr_tail can carry only the last stderr line (scratch path), never config or env, because the target selftest reads neither.
findings.evidence: evidence/receipt-field-inventory.json marker_scan and pointed_line_bytes_in_receipts; in-memory scan, no content written
findings.impact: Compliant with the security bound as written.
findings.remediation: If the conditional stderr_tail is kept for future targets, store its sha256 and line count instead of the raw line.

findings.finding: line_sha256 hashes the decoded text (open(..., errors="replace") + readlines + join), so it is the raw line bytes only for UTF-8/LF files. A CRLF or non-UTF-8 pointed file would digest a normalised line, and the selftest only exercises ASCII/LF.
findings.evidence: pointer-bind.py:115-121,105; selftest cases green-line/green-range use "\n" strings
findings.impact: None for the five live files (all UTF-8/LF); a future pointer could claim a digest that is not a byte digest.
findings.remediation: Read bytes, split on b"\n", digest the raw slice; or state the normalisation in the docstring.

findings.finding: git_show interpolates rev as f"{rev}:{path}" into a single argv after `git -C <root> show` (both instruments). rev is not validated as a commit name, so a leading "--" makes git parse the operand as an option rather than <rev>:<path>.
findings.impact: Not reachable in the wave (callers pass 40-hex); an adversarial caller controlling --rev could at best make git error or, with option shapes, misparse; no execution path demonstrated.
findings.remediation: Reject --rev unless it matches ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ before the call.
